title: Your own picture: the input folder, LoadImage and its mask

questions.q: You load a JPEG of 800 by 600. What is the shape of the MASK output?
questions.why: With no alpha channel LoadImage returns a 64 by 64 mask of zeros, whatever the picture's size. A real run confirmed it.

questions.q: In a PNG with transparency, what does a mask value of 1 mean?
options: That pixel is fully transparent in the file
That pixel is fully opaque in the file
questions.answer: That pixel is fully transparent in the file

questions.q: You save over your picture with a new one under the same name, and queue again. Does LoadImage re-read it?
options: Yes: its change check hashes the file's bytes
No: only the name is in the cache key
questions.answer: Yes: its change check hashes the file's bytes
questions.why: IS_CHANGED returns a SHA-256 of the file. A checkpoint loader has no such hook (CU-102).

questions.q: Why does a 3024 by 4032 phone photo take so long in an img2img graph built for 512 by 512?
options: LoadImage keeps every pixel, so the latent is far larger than the model expects
Phone photos use a special format
The VAE refuses it and retries forever
questions.answer: LoadImage keeps every pixel, so the latent is far larger than the model expects
questions.why: Nothing resizes for you. The lab gives a latent of [1, 4, 504, 378], with 46.5 times the pixels of 512 by 512. Scale it first (CU-109).
